_comment: What syncs from baseline to each Core, what's per-Core, what each Core adds on top. Spec: tasks/spec-self-hosted-cores-2026-05-19.md Phase 7.
_baseline_writer_comment: Single-writer policy (2026-06-02): only this Core may PUSH shared code to the baseline. All other Cores are pull-only — they sync FROM baseline but never TO it, so they can't clobber each other's edits. Enforced by sync-to-baseline.sh (aborts on non-writer; override with --force-writer) and queue-shared-push.sh (no push marker on non-writer Cores). Override exists for the rare case a shared fix is authored inside another Core.
_per_core_keep_state_comment: .claude/state/** is a Core's own learned layer, telemetry and markers — active.json, friction artifacts, hook-events.log, session markers. It survived sync until 2026-07-27 only BY ACCIDENT: the contents are gitignored and the orphan-delete pass is bounded to scheduling/, so the path was simply out of scope rather than protected. Widen that pass for any unrelated reason and every Core's learned state becomes deletable. Declared explicitly so the protection is a decision rather than a coincidence.
_per_core_extras_comment: Files a specific Core adds on top of the shared set. Entries are globs, not literal names — this manifest ships to every Core and to any fork, so a real person's name in a path here is published. Generalized 2026-07-27.
_retired_comment: TOMBSTONES — paths the baseline has RETIRED, which pullers must delete. rsync in sync-from-baseline.sh is `rsync -a` with NO --delete (additive by design), and the orphan-cleanup pass is bounded to scheduling/ and driven by THIS manifest's shared.dirs, never by a baseline deletion. So a `git rm` on the baseline removes a file there and NOWHERE ELSE: core-finance measured 6 retired files still sitting on 3-4 peer seats on 2026-08-13, the oldest retired 2026-05-15. Listing a path here is the only way a deletion travels. A LIST, deliberately, and not `rsync --delete`: --delete removes anything in the destination absent from the source, so one imperfect exclude would take a peer's per_core_keep data with it. A tombstone can only ever remove exactly what is named. Entries are safe to keep forever and are no-ops once every seat has pulled once. CENSUS 2026-08-13: `git log --diff-filter=D` over every shared path found 55 paths ever deleted from a shared location and still absent on the writer. Only these six are listed, DELIBERATELY. The other 49 are per-run artifacts that merely live under a shared dir — ~20 compile-truth-work/refresh-batch-*.json, ~15 graphify checkpoints, .bak scratch — and several are already covered by per_core_keep globs, so a tombstone would be refused anyway. The bar for an entry is VERIFIED RETIRED SHARED CODE, not 'absent from git': a tombstone is a fleet-wide unattended delete. The census also surfaced .claude/agents/sentinel/CLAUDE.md and sentinel-code/CLAUDE.md in the deleted-upstream list — they are per_core_keep trust roots deliberately still present, and listing them would have been catastrophic. That is what the glob-aware per_core_keep refusal in sync-from-baseline.sh exists to stop.
